content.text: Building it now; the sketch-edge axis didn't resolve, so I'm moving the rod off-origin so I can revolve about the sketch's own V axis instead.

I built the J-hook as one valid solid and exported it to `submission.step`. The file was read back after export and matched the part.

**What it's made of:**
- A square base plate, 80 × 80 mm and 8 mm thick.
- A round rod, 20 mm across, standing straight up from the centre of the plate to a height of 140 mm.
- A half-circle hook on top of the rod, made by sweeping the rod's cross-section around a 55 mm radius. It curls toward −X and ends pointing down. Overall the part is about 165 × 80 × 210 mm.

**Comparison with the target:** I rendered the same four camera views and checked them against `composite.png`. The orientation matches in all four, including which way the hook curls. The only differences I can see are small: in the target, the plate looks slightly larger and the rod slightly thicker compared with the hook. I didn't adjust for these.

I took the sizes from the image by eye, so they're estimates. Absolute size isn't scored; only the proportions matter.
